title: Financial Crises and Public Finances: Crisis Preparedness for Government
summary: An eight-module advanced programme preparing finance ministries and senior officials to manage financial crises, protect public finances and coordinate resolution.
intro: This training programme equips finance ministries and senior officials to prepare for and manage financial crises: understanding resolution regimes and safety nets, limiting the use of public funds, coordinating authorities and communicating under pressure.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give the officials who will take decisions in a financial crisis a practical understanding of the crisis management toolkit, the finance ministry's role within it and the fiscal stakes involved. Participants leave able to assess national preparedness, take informed decisions on resolution and public support, coordinate with domestic and foreign authorities, and lead a credible crisis response under time pressure.
sections.What It Covers: How financial crises unfold and their fiscal costs, the finance ministry's role in crisis management, resolution regimes and the FSB Key Attributes, bail-in and loss allocation, deposit insurance and investor protection, public support, guarantees and state aid, liquidity support and funding in resolution, domestic and cross-border crisis management groups, simulations, and crisis communication.
Intended Audience: Senior officials in finance ministries and treasuries with responsibility for financial stability and crisis management
Members and secretariats of national financial stability and crisis management committees
Legal, fiscal and communications advisers who would support ministers in a financial crisis
Learning Objectives: Explain how financial crises develop and the channels through which they hit public finances
Define the finance ministry's role and decision rights in a financial crisis
Assess the national resolution regime, safety nets and funding arrangements against international standards
Evaluate when and how public support should be provided and how losses should be allocated
Design effective domestic and cross-border crisis coordination arrangements
Lead crisis decision-making and communication through a realistic simulation
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as an intensive programme over two to three days or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a briefing with crisis case studies and decision exercises, culminating in a full crisis simulation, and modules can be selected or tailored to the national crisis management framework.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Experience of financial stability, fiscal or financial sector policy is helpful. No prior crisis management experience is required.
Core Reading: FSB (2014), Key Attributes of Effective Resolution Regimes for Financial Institutions
IADI (2014), IADI Core Principles for Effective Deposit Insurance Systems
FSB (2016), Guiding Principles on the Temporary Funding Needed to Support the Orderly Resolution of a Global Systemically Important Bank

modules.title: Anatomy of a Financial Crisis
modules.summary: How banking, market and sovereign crises develop, the warning signs that precede them, and the channels through which they damage public finances and the wider economy.
objectives: Explain the main types and triggers of financial crises
Identify the bank-sovereign doom loop and other fiscal transmission channels
Draw lessons from historical and recent crises
syllabus: Bank runs, contagion, fire sales and liquidity spirals
Fiscal costs of crises and contingent liabilities
The bank-sovereign nexus and market confidence
Case studies of systemic and idiosyncratic failures

modules.title: Crisis Management Architecture and the Finance Ministry
modules.summary: How responsibilities are divided between the finance ministry, central bank, resolution authority, supervisor and deposit insurer, and how decisions are taken when public funds may be at risk.
objectives: Map the roles and legal powers of each authority in a crisis
Define the finance ministry's decision rights and veto points
Assess the adequacy of national coordination committees and protocols
syllabus: Financial safety net participants and their mandates
Decision rights where public funds or fiscal risk are involved
Financial stability and crisis management committees
Memoranda of understanding, protocols and escalation

modules.title: Resolution Regimes and the Key Attributes
modules.summary: What an effective resolution regime contains, how resolution tools work, and how government can assess whether the national regime meets the FSB Key Attributes.
objectives: Explain the purpose of resolution and its objectives
Describe the main resolution tools and powers
Assess the national regime and resolution planning against the Key Attributes
syllabus: Resolution objectives and the public interest test
Sale of business, bridge institutions, asset separation and bail-in
Resolution planning, resolvability and loss-absorbing capacity
Resolution of insurers, central counterparties and non-banks

modules.title: Bail-In, Loss Allocation and Public Support
modules.summary: How losses are allocated to shareholders and creditors through bail-in, when public support may be justified, and how to design it to protect taxpayers and limit moral hazard.
objectives: Explain the creditor hierarchy and no-creditor-worse-off safeguard
Evaluate the conditions for public support and the instruments available
Design safeguards to recover public funds and limit moral hazard
syllabus: Bail-in mechanics, execution and market impact
Recapitalisation, guarantees, asset purchases and nationalisation
State aid principles, burden sharing and conditionality
Recovering public funds and exit from public ownership

modules.title: Deposit Insurance and Investor Protection
modules.summary: How deposit insurance and investor compensation schemes protect consumers and confidence, how they are funded, and how they interact with resolution.
objectives: Explain the design features of an effective deposit insurance system
Assess coverage, funding and payout speed against IADI Core Principles
Evaluate the role of investor and policyholder protection schemes
syllabus: Coverage levels, scope and depositor preference
Ex ante and ex post funding and government backstops
Payout readiness and the use of funds in resolution
Investor compensation and policyholder protection schemes

modules.title: Liquidity Support and Funding in Resolution
modules.summary: How central bank liquidity, government guarantees and resolution funds provide temporary funding in a crisis, and how to protect the public balance sheet when doing so.
objectives: Distinguish market-wide liquidity, emergency liquidity assistance and resolution funding
Assess the role of fiscal backstops and indemnities
Evaluate the risks to the central bank and public balance sheets
syllabus: Lender of last resort and emergency liquidity assistance
Resolution funds and temporary public sector funding mechanisms
Government guarantees of liabilities and their fiscal cost
Collateral, indemnities and protecting the public balance sheet

modules.title: Cross-Border Coordination and Crisis Communication
modules.summary: How authorities cooperate when a failing group spans borders, and how ministers and officials communicate with markets, depositors, parliament and the public during a crisis.
objectives: Explain the role of crisis management groups and cooperation agreements
Anticipate cross-border conflicts over losses, assets and timing
Design a crisis communication strategy and key messages
syllabus: Crisis management groups and institution-specific cooperation agreements
Home and host tensions, ring-fencing and burden sharing
Communication with markets, depositors, media and parliament
Weekend resolution: timing, announcements and market opening

modules.title: Crisis Simulation and Preparedness Planning
modules.summary: Brings the programme together in a realistic crisis simulation in which participants take decisions under time pressure, followed by a review of national preparedness and an action plan.
objectives: Apply the crisis toolkit to a realistic failing-institution scenario
Identify gaps in powers, information, funding and coordination
Produce a national crisis preparedness action plan
syllabus: Designing and running crisis simulation exercises
Simulation: a failing systemic institution over a resolution weekend
Debrief: decisions, information gaps and coordination lessons
Workshop: a national crisis preparedness action plan

related.title: Financial Services Policy Essentials for Government
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving government officials a clear grounding in the financial system, regulatory architecture, international standards and the policy levers government holds.

related.title: Financial Services Regulation: A Briefing Programme for Parliamentarians
related.summary: A six-module, non-technical briefing programme helping parliamentarians and committee staff scrutinise financial legislation and hold regulators to account.

related.title: AI in Financial Services: Policy Choices for Government
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping policymakers understand AI in financial services and make informed choices on regulation, institutional roles and national strategy.

related.title: Developing Capital Markets and Investment Fund Industries
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping policymakers develop deep, well-regulated capital markets and fund industries through credible, well-sequenced reform.
